headline: 3 DNCC trucks torched, police vehicle vandalised in Mirpur eviction drive clash
summary: Violence erupted in Mirpur-10 as hawkers and traders allegedly set fire to city corporation vehicles during a drive to clear illegal structures.
details: A police vehicle was vandalised and three Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) garbage trucks were set on fire during an eviction drive in Dhaka's Mirpur-10 today.
The incident occurred as DNCC authorities were conducting a drive to clear illegal structures and hawker stalls from footpaths in the area.
According to officials and witnesses, hawkers and roadside traders allegedly set fire to the three garbage trucks.
They also allegedly vandalised an excavator and a police vehicle during the clash.
Two units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence were deployed to bring the flames under control.
The exact extent of the damage and whether anyone was injured could not be immediately confirmed.
DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan is scheduled to brief journalists on the matter shortly.
caption:
3 city corporation trucks torched and a police vehicle vandalised in Mirpur-10 during a footpath eviction drive.

A police vehicle was vandalised and three Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) garbage trucks were set on fire during an eviction drive in Dhaka's Mirpur-10 today.

The incident occurred as DNCC authorities were conducting a drive to clear illegal structures and hawker stalls from footpaths in the area.

According to officials and witnesses, hawkers and roadside traders allegedly set fire to the three garbage trucks.

They also allegedly vandalised an excavator and a police vehicle during the clash.

Two units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence were deployed to bring the flames under control.

The exact extent of the damage and whether anyone was injured could not be immediately confirmed.

DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan is scheduled to brief journalists on the matter shortly.

headline_marked: Woman in Magura gets [[electricity bill of 506 crore BDT]], corrected to 1,963 BDT
headline: Woman in Magura gets electricity bill of 506 crore BDT, corrected to 1,963 BDT
summary: A residential consumer in Magura was billed over 506 crore BDT for using only 235 units of electricity, leading to the dismissal of the Palli Bidyut Samity's GM.
details: A residential consumer named Mst. Aleya Khatun from Kechuadubi village in Magura's Moghi Union received a shocking electricity bill of 506 crore 83 lakh 11 thousand 593 BDT.
The bill, issued by the Arpara Zonal Office of Magura Palli Bidyut Samity, was for the use of only 235 units of electricity in a single month.
The total amount included a base bill of 482 crore 69 lakh 63 thousand 422 BDT and VAT of 24 crore 13 lakh 48 thousand 171 BDT.
Following the incident, the General Manager (GM) of Magura Palli Bidyut Samity was immediately dismissed from his post.
Four other staff members have been issued show-cause notices to explain the massive clerical error.
The Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku, personally called the consumer to express his apologies.
The error was later corrected, and the consumer paid the actual bill of 1,963 BDT.
The Deputy General Manager (DGM) of the Arpara Zonal Office, Md. Rezaul Karim, confirmed that while the meter units were correct, the billing copy was erroneous.
caption:
Imagine getting a bill for 506 crore BDT for using just 235 units of electricity. This happened to a woman in Magura.

A residential consumer named Mst. Aleya Khatun from Kechuadubi village in Magura's Moghi Union received a shocking electricity bill of 506 crore 83 lakh 11 thousand 593 BDT.

The bill, issued by the Arpara Zonal Office of Magura Palli Bidyut Samity, was for the use of only 235 units of electricity in a single month.

The total amount included a base bill of 482 crore 69 lakh 63 thousand 422 BDT and VAT of 24 crore 13 lakh 48 thousand 171 BDT.

Following the incident, the General Manager (GM) of Magura Palli Bidyut Samity was immediately dismissed from his post.

Four other staff members have been issued show-cause notices to explain the massive clerical error.

The Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku, personally called the consumer to express his apologies.

The error was later corrected, and the consumer paid the actual bill of 1,963 BDT.

The Deputy General Manager (DGM) of the Arpara Zonal Office, Md. Rezaul Karim, confirmed that while the meter units were correct, the billing copy was erroneous.
